hypotheses.justification: The proof (through `prod_measure_diff_eq_zero_of_ae_ae_restrict_section₀`) uses `hs` only once: to get measurability of the section `s_x = {y | (x, y) ∈ s}`, so that it can rewrite with `Measure.restrict_apply_eq_zero'`. That step works without measurability. Mathlib's `Measure.le_restrict_apply (s t : Set α) : μ (t ∩ s) ≤ μ.restrict s t` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Restrict.lean) holds for arbitrary sets. For each x, `hsection x` unfolds through `ae_iff` to `ν.restrict s_x {y | (x, y) ∉ G} = 0`. So `ν ({y | (x, y) ∉ G} ∩ s_x) ≤ 0`, and this set is `Prod.mk x ⁻¹' (s \ G)`, so the section of `s \ G` at every x is ν-null. The rest of the proof is unchanged. `hbad.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq` gives a measurable `t ⊆ s \ G` with `t =ᵐ s \ G`. Each section of `t` sits inside the null section of `s \ G`, so `measure_mono` makes it null. Then `Measure.measure_prod_null htmeas` (it needs only `SFinite ν` and measurability of `t`) gives `μ.prod ν t = 0`, and `measure_congr` gives `μ.prod ν (s \ G) = 0`. There are no degenerate cases: the argument holds for every x and needs nothing about s. Note that `hbad` itself cannot be removed. In ZFC there is a graph of a function [0,1]→[0,1] with full outer Lebesgue measure; taking s = univ and G its complement, every vertical section of s \ G is a single point, yet its product measure is positive.
